config.title: React.memo

intro.title: React.memo
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue application to understand how to optimize component rendering, similar to the concept of React.memo in React. You will learn how to prevent unnecessary re-renders of child components when their props haven't changed, improving performance. The core concept involves using Vue's built-in reactivity system and the `v-once` directive or computed properties for memoization. You'll work with Vue components, props, and directives to implement this optimization. This lesson will help you write more efficient Vue applications by controlling when components update.
intro.usecase: In real-world Vue applications, you often need to prevent unnecessary re-renders of child components to maintain performance, especially in data-heavy interfaces. This is crucial in dashboards with live-updating charts, large e-commerce product filters, or complex data tables where parent state changes frequently but child components receive static or unchanged props. By properly implementing memoization (using `computed` properties, `watch` with careful dependencies, or tools like `v-memo` in Vue 3), developers ensure that UI components like sidebars, modals, or form inputs only update when their specific data changes, leading to smoother user interactions and efficient resource use.

objectives: Implement a basic Vue component that demonstrates unnecessary re-renders
Apply the `computed` property to create memoized values in Vue components
Configure component options to optimize rendering using Vue's reactivity system
Manipulate component data to trigger re-renders and observe performance differences
Integrate watch properties with computed properties for complex memoization scenarios
Construct a parent-child component structure to demonstrate prop-based re-rendering
Control component updates by implementing proper dependency tracking in computed properties

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named App with a template and script setup. The template should contain a root div element.
steps.hint: Use the <template> tag for the template and <script setup> for the script. The template should have a single root element, like a div.

steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named App is created with a template containing a root div and a script setup section.
successCriteria: The App component has a template with a root div element and a script setup section.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the template has a root div element and the script uses setup.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component structure is incorrect. Check that you have a template with a root div and a script setup section.

steps.title: Initialize reactive state for counter
steps.instruction: Inside the <script setup> section, use defineReactive to create a reactive counter state with an initial value of 0.
steps.hint: Use defineReactive to make a variable reactive. The syntax is: defineReactive(variableName, initialValue).
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating reactive state
const count = defineReactive(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a reactive counter state initialized to 0, ready to be used in the template.
successCriteria: A reactive counter variable is created using defineReactive with initial value 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using defineReactive with the correct syntax and initial value of 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: use defineReactive inside the <script setup> section to create a reactive counter with initial value 0.

steps.title: Create increment handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the <script setup> section, create a function named increment that increases the counter value by 1.
steps.hint: Define a function that modifies the reactive counter variable. In Vue with <script setup>, you can define functions directly.
steps.expectedOutcome: The increment function is defined and will be used to update the counter state in a later step.
successCriteria: A function named increment is defined that increases the counter value by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a function named 'increment' that modifies the counter variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The increment function isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a function with the right name and update logic.

steps.title: Add counter display to template
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a paragraph element that displays the current counter value.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to display reactive state values in the template.
steps.analogousExample: // Displaying a reactive value in template
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now includes a paragraph that shows the current counter value.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists in the template that displays the counter value using {{ counter }}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but make sure it displays the counter value using {{ counter }}.

steps.hint: Use the @click directive to attach the click event handler to the button.

// Example: button with click handler
<button @click="handleClick">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button that increments the counter when clicked appears below the counter display.
successCriteria: The template contains a button element with @click="incrementCounter".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it calls incrementCounter when clicked using @click.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly wired to the incrementCounter function.

steps.title: Create a child component for demonstration
steps.instruction: Create a new Vue component named 'ChildComponent' that accepts a prop called 'message' and displays it in a paragraph.
steps.hint: In Vue's <script setup>, you can define a component as a function or const that returns a template. Use defineProps to declare the message prop.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ChildComponent is defined that can receive and display a message prop.
successCriteria: ChildComponent is defined with a message prop and displays it in a paragraph.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the component, but make sure it accepts a 'message' prop and displays it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Ensure you create a ChildComponent that accepts a message prop.

steps.title: Pass data from parent to child component
steps.instruction: Render the ChildComponent inside the template and pass a message prop with the value 'Hello from parent'.
steps.hint: Add the ChildComponent as a self-closing tag in the template and use the prop syntax to pass the message.
steps.analogousExample:
// Passing a prop to a child component
<ChildComponent message="Hello from parent" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildComponent will be rendered in the App with the message prop passed from the parent.
successCriteria: ChildComponent is rendered in the template with a message prop set to 'Hello from parent'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're rendering ChildComponent and passing the message prop correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ChildComponent isn't rendered or the prop isn't passed. Check the template syntax.

steps.title: Add console.log to child component
steps.instruction: Inside your ChildComponent, add a console.log statement that will execute every time the component renders.
steps.hint: Place console.log('ChildComponent rendered') at the beginning of the component's setup function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildComponent will log a message to the console each time it renders, allowing you to observe re-renders.
successCriteria: ChildComponent contains a console.log statement that executes on every render.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the console.log statement is placed inside the ChildComponent function so it executes every time the component renders.
steps.feedbackWrong: The console.log statement should be added inside the ChildComponent function, not outside of it. Try adding console.log('ChildComponent rendered') at the beginning of the component.

steps.title: Wrap child component with Vue.memo
steps.instruction: Wrap your ChildComponent function with Vue.memo to memoize it and prevent unnecessary re-renders.
steps.hint: Use Vue.memo() to wrap the component function before using it in the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildComponent will be memoized, preventing re-renders when its props haven't changed.
successCriteria: ChildComponent is wrapped with Vue.memo and the component still renders correctly.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're wrapping the entire ChildComponent function with Vue.memo, not just calling it.
